node.title: Re^3: Converting UTF8 to ANSI
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
You may want to have a look at [https://www.joelonsoftware.com/2003/10/08/the-absolute-minimum-every-software-developer-absolutely-positively-must-know-about-unicode-and-character-sets-no-excuses/|The Absolute Minimum Every Software Developer Absolutely, Positively Must Know About Unicode and Character Sets (No Excuses!)]

As for what I mean by ANSI, I really don't know. All I know is what the encoding line says when I "save as" a file with "Notepad" (Win-xp).

I suspect that'll be an encoding like the one I mentioned. You could use the other module I [id://1198033|showed], [doc://Encode::Guess], to try and find out - it's a core module, no installation necessary. Another trick is to use a character that gets encoded differently in different encodings. I like the Euro symbol € ("\x{20AC}" in Perl), other than being easy to type on my keyboard, it is:

  • Not representable in [wp://ASCII#Character_set|ASCII] or [wp://ISO/IEC_8859-1#Code_page_layout|Latin1 (aka ISO/IEC 8859-1)]
  • In [wp://ISO/IEC_8859-15#Codepage_layout|Latin-9 (aka ISO/IEC 8859-15)] it is the byte 0xA4
  • In [wp://Windows-1252#Character_set|Windows-1252 (aka CP-1252 and sometimes aka "ANSI")] it is the byte 0x80
  • In [wp://Mac_OS_Roman#Codepage_layout|MacRoman] it is the byte 0xDB (at least Mac OS >=8.5)
  • In [wp://UTF-8] it is the bytes 0xE2, 0x82, 0xAC
  • In [wp://UTF-16] it is 0x20AC - depending on endianness, bytes 0x20, 0xAC in UTF-16-BE, or 0xAC, 0x20 in UTF-16-LE

So try typing "€" into Notepad, saving it, and using a hex editor to get a clue (not a definite answer) as to what encoding it is.

Minor updates.
